messages:
Anita: Heads-up — billing alert showed a huge spike overnight, ~ $62k/day for the cluster costs. ops-bot flagged massive scale events in us-west1-gpu-pool. Anyone seeing this?
ops-bot: [ALERT] cost_spike detected for project-redwood-inference · estimated_daily = $62,134 · triggered_by = autoscaler · resource = us-west1-gpu-pool · events = 418 scale_up ops in last 6h
Sam: whoa. Thanks for the ping. Can you paste the autoscaler events / nodepool template?
Anita: Copying the relevant events and nodepool YAML we grabbed from the control plane logs.
Anita: ```
Event 2026-11-02T03:12:11Z: autoscaler scale up: adding 40 nodes (requested 40), reason: insufficient gpus for podset
Event 2026-11-02T03:13:02Z: autoscaler scale up: adding 60 nodes, reason: pending pods with gpu request
... repeated ~7h ...
NodePool template: 
  machineType: n2-custom-16-122880
  accelerator: { type: nvidia-tesla-v100, count: 1 }
  labels: { pool: gpu, runtime: redwood-runtime }
  taints: []
```
Sam: Hmm. The template shows `nvidia-tesla-v100` for accelerators but our infra repo uses `a2`-family for A100s. That mismatch could cause scheduler to pick different instances or fall back to on-demand pools. Did a recent infra roll change the var for gpu_family?
Jasper: I just pulled the latest infra deploy — there was a renaming of the var `gpu_profile` to `gpu_family` in commit 4f3a2c last night (PR #3124). Looks like the default value got reset to "v100-legacy" while the pool selector expects `a100`.
Keiko: That would explain cost: we have commitments for A100 in committed use discounts (CUDs) in us-west1 but if nodes launched as V100 or as non-committed on-demand types the CUDs won't apply. Billing would revert to full on-demand rates.
Sam: Can you show the terraform snippet? Need to confirm the var drift.
Anita: ```hcl
variable "gpu_family" {
  type = string
  default = "v100-legacy" # <- oops, used to be "a100-sxm" in previous releases
}
resource "google_compute_instance_template" "gpu" {
  machine_type = var.machine_type
  guest_accelerator {
    type  = var.gpu_family
    count = var.gpu_count
  }
}
```
Sam: Yep that's the problem. CI didn't catch it because we only validate machine_type, not accelerator SKUs. The autoscaler created node templates that matched the wrong GPU SKU and the cloud provider fell back to the closest available SKU (on-demand V100 clusters in a different zone) — hence huge cost and also provisioning thrash.
Jasper: Also noticed autoscaler max_unavailable was misconfigured so it aggressively spun up new nodepools instead of reusing reserved capacity. Combined effects = new on-demand pools + wrong SKU.
Keiko: Immediate ask from Finance: reduce burn now. Any chance to scale down to reserved pools and stop new on-demand launches?
Sam: Steps I'm running now:
- cordon and drain newly-created nodepools created after 2026-11-02T00:00 UTC
- patch autoscaler policy to not create new nodepools (set max_nodes to current)
- rollout corrected instance template with `gpu_family = "a100-sxm"` and a CI check to validate accelerator SKU vs commitments
Anita: Commands I'm running now:
```bash
# list nodes created after cutoff
kubectl get nodes --show-labels | grep us-west1 | awk '{print $1, $5}' > /tmp/usw-nodes.txt
# cordon + drain loop
for n in $(cat /tmp/usw-nodes.txt); do kubectl cordon $n; kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -t 30s || true; done
```
Sam: I've applied a temporary autoscaler patch to freeze new nodepool creation: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling --no-autoscaling --region us-west1 <group>` for the suspect groups. That will stop further launches while we fix templates.
Keiko: Good. Please also open a support case with the cloud rep — we should ask for retroactive credits for the instance-family mismatch; we'll need the incident timeline. I'll prepare the billing timeline once you confirm nodes that ran and their SKUs.
Jasper: Filing ticket INFRA-3421 with the root cause and immediate mitigation steps. Adding owners: @Sam, @Anita, @Keiko.
Anita: Quick action note: found ~412 nodes launched between 00:00–06:30 UTC, estimated excess cost ~ $48k. Most were spun up in us-west1-b as on-demand V100 attachments while our CUDs are for A100 in us-west1-a.
Sam: For long-term fix: add these checks
- CI unit that verifies `var.gpu_family` aligns with reserved SKUs for the region
- autotest that simulates scale-up with the autoscaler and checks node template SKU
- change autoscaler policy to prefer existing reserved pools (tagging + affinity)
Jasper: Also adding a monitoring rule: alert if nodepools created in >3 different zones in a 1h window for the same pool label (likely runaway scaling).
Keiko: Finance will pause some non-critical spend lines and flag this to execs; if cloud vendor gives credits, we'll allocate to this quarter.
Anita: Post-mortem checklist:
- writeup in docs (link INFRA-3421)
- revert the var default to the safe value in staging + prod
- CI SKU validation added to PR gate
- follow-up with cloud rep for credits
Sam: Done with cordon/drain for the newest nodepools. Autoscaler paused. Patching terraform now and will run a controlled rolling update to replace templates.
Anita: Thanks everyone. Will monitor billing dashboard and post updates here. :eyes:
Keiko: Please add expected timeline for rollback + cost estimate to INFRA-3421 by EOD.
Jasper: I'll own the CI test. Sam will own the patch. Anita will own the monitoring and outage timeline. ops-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated (scale frozen).
Anita: last note — let's add a guard in deploy pipeline that rejects var defaults that diverge from `committed_gpu_skus` mapping. Learned this the hard way.
Sam: Agreed. Also let's schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow to lock in follow-ups. :thumbsup:
